collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Every household brings its favorite dish to the shared-labor festival and the arguments begin: judge the dishes, or just eat.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The big harvest project is finished, and every household is bringing its favorite dish to the festival of shared labor. (subject) and (friend) have already argued about whose fish stew is better, and so have six other families. Someone has suggested judging. What should happen?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The judging takes all evening and nearly causes three feuds. The winner is a dish nobody expected: a grandmother's plain boiled taro. The losers grumble and eat seconds of it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Nobody judges. Everyone eats everything. (subject) and (friend) try each other's stew and each admit, after a lot of chewing, that the other one is good. Not better. Good.
